title: Secondary Bounded Rationality: A Theory of How Algorithms Reproduce Structural Inequality in AI Hiring

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical analysis applying Bourdieusian capital theory to evaluate how AI hiring algorithms codify tacit cultural hierarchies into technical features, such as penalizing non-standard communication styles (e.g., African American Vernacular English) and over-representing elite university credentials.

Conceptual evaluation using sociological network theories (e.g., Granovetter's weak ties, Burt's structural holes) to demonstrate how recruitment algorithms prioritize quantifiable, strong-tie network metrics, thereby marginalizing candidates who lack dominant-group social capital.

Literature synthesis and theoretical modeling illustrating how predictive AI inherits path-dependent historical biases, using examples such as algorithms that disadvantage women by prioritizing predicted tenure based on historically disparate turnover rates.
